White Paper Builder v1.1

Cover

Cover photo

The photo fills the whole cover, to every edge. Upright, and at least 1700 pixels wide, prints best. The name and date sit on a dark fade at the bottom.

Inside

The sources print on the last page, numbered in the order they are first cited.

Look

Cover

Cover image

A map, diagram, or photo, about 7 × 1.7 inches. Optional.

Series and publisher

Look

One page, about 300 words. Notes and citations work here too.

What is happening, and why it will still matter in five years. A blank line starts a new paragraph.

The main claim, the strongest evidence, and the consequence readers are most likely to miss. Numbered 01, 02, 03.

Who should act, and what they should do. Numbered R1, R2, R3.

How to write the body

Charts, tables, timelines, key numbers, and images. Give each one a short name, then place it in the body or an appendix with [[name]] on a line of its own. Figures and tables are numbered in the order they appear.

Each # heading starts Appendix A, B, C. ## headings are numbered A.1, A.2. [[rating-key]] adds the source rating key table.

Cite sources from your OSINT Citation Generator lists. In the generator, save your list to a file; open that file here. Each source gets a short key.

Write [@key] or [@key, p. 45] in the text: the first citation of a source prints in full in a footnote, later ones in short form.

Write [@key] in a story where you use the source. Nothing prints there: the source joins the numbered list on the last page, in order of first citation. [ORIGINAL STORY: @key] puts that label in front of its entry.

Use *asterisks* for italics. A page number in [@key, p. 4] goes before the final period.

No sources yet. You can still write notes by hand with ^[note text].

The "Cite as" line is built from the title, author, number, version, publisher, date, and link under Paper.
